clue.text: Funding that women tend to organise

indicators.note: to organise is to put into a new arrangement, so the preceding words are rearranged

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: A grant that women tend to arrange among themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment is money given to provide an income for an institution, i.e. a source of funding.

clue.text: Cries over climaxes

indicators.note: turned over, the letters fall into a different order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone sobs over the high points of a story.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to call out suddenly, so someone who exclaims cries out.

clue.text: Order the stonework

blocks.note: surface reading: a command to buy masonry
setter's reading: one of the classical styles of columns seen in Greek stonework

explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a verb, a command to a builder; it is the noun for a style of classical architecture, the plainest of the Greek ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is one of the classical architectural orders, with plain capitals, seen in temple stonework like the Parthenon.

clue.text: One who forecasts the need for topper here — what nonsense!

indicators.note: nonsense is jumbled sense, so the letters before it are scrambled

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
taken letter for letter, also part of the signal

explanation.surface: Someone predicting that a top hat will be required, dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a forecaster saying a hat (a topper) will be needed for rain or sun; 'what' does double duty as fodder and part of the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather prophet predicts the weather, a jocular old term for a forecaster.

clue.text: Makes possible European prohibition over the French

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom up

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a ban is a prohibition
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: EU rules permit a ban to override French practice.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable something is to make it possible, so enables is a direct synonym of makes possible.

clue.text: Propose gold to create dramatic scene

blocks.note: to table a motion is to propose it
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Suggesting golden staging to make a scene dramatic.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage, to table a motion means to put it forward; in America it means the opposite, to shelve it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking group of people arranged as if in a picture, a dramatic scene.

clue.text: Said to be marque of second vehicle

definitions.note: sounds like 'mark', which is what the answer is

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A rumour about the brand of someone's second car.
explanation.walkthrough: A marque is a car brand, but the definition works by sound: 'said to be marque' means a homophone of it, a mark, and a scar is a mark on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a lasting mark left on skin by a healed wound, and mark sounds like marque.

clue.text: Alluring girl includes touch of rosemary in potato cake

indicators.note: just a touch of a word is its very first letter
something that includes another holds it inside

blocks.note: a coquette is a flirtatious woman
the first letter

explanation.surface: A flirt adds a hint of rosemary to a potato cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A croquette is a small cake of mashed potato or minced food, coated in breadcrumbs and fried.

clue.text: Trust Edward's heart to become oxidised

indicators.note: the heart of the phrase is its inner part, where the letters lie

blocks.note: the inner letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: Trusting Edward's good nature will see it wear away.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust is iron oxide, so iron that has rusted has become oxidised.

clue.text: Blacklegs hit emergency circuit switchs

blocks.note: to strike is to hit
circuit breakers cut the power in an emergency

explanation.surface: Strikebreakers hit the emergency switches.
explanation.walkthrough: Blacklegs is British slang for workers who cross a picket line.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackleg is a worker who carries on during a strike, so blacklegs are strikebreakers.

clue.text: American agents surround old town court

indicators.note: agents that surround something enclose it, so the other piece sits inside them

blocks.note: the Central Intelligence Agency
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, the crossword's favourite old town

explanation.surface: US spies close in on a court in some old town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Curia is the papal court and administration in Rome; historically the word means a court of justice.

clue.text: A pound sorts a problem out for the winger

indicators.note: letters sorted out are put back in a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pays a pound to fix a difficulty for a footballer on the wing.
explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings flank the wordplay: an albatross is a burden or problem (from The Rime of the Ancient Mariner) and also a great seabird, 'the winger'.
explanation.definitionFit: The albatross is a large seabird with huge wings, and figuratively a burden that hangs round one's neck.

clue.text: Every one accepts company house needs hard liquor

indicators.note: something that accepts another thing takes it inside itself

blocks.note: every one of them is all of them
Co is the abbreviation for company
ho is an abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Everyone at the firm's house party wants strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard liquor is spirits, the strongest kind of alcohol, so the general word covers it.

clue.text: Oriental film has no time for person of taste

indicators.note: having no time means the abbreviation for time is taken out

blocks.note: E for East, the Orient
a picture is a film
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An Eastern movie with no slot in the schedule for a connoisseur.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the T from PICTURE before putting E in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is someone with refined taste, especially a connoisseur of food and wine.

clue.text: Must trend at English university be to produce older pupil?

indicators.note: the words are made to produce something new, i.e. their letters are rearranged into it

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
E is the abbreviation for English
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A question about whether fashions at an English university must produce older students.
explanation.definitionFit: A mature student is one who enters higher education later in life than usual, hence an older pupil.

clue.text: Current movement treated WI appallingly

indicators.note: something done appallingly is badly messed up, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A modern campaign that mistreated the Women's Institute.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidewater is water carried by the tide, so it is literally a current moving in and out.

clue.text: Kilts are in fashion for aspiring models

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; this phrase describes what aspiring models wish to be

indicators.note: fashioned words are shaped anew, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Kilts are trendy among would-be fashion models.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspiring models hope to become celebrities, so they want to look like stars, i.e. starlike.

clue.text: Put on a show of up-to-date kind of electricity

blocks.note: to direct a play is to put on a show
current means up to date

explanation.surface: Stage a show featuring a modern kind of electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Direct current is electrical flow in one direction only, as from a battery, as opposed to alternating current.

clue.text: It is added willingly

blocks.note: surface reading: something given gladly
setter's reading: tacked onto a will

explanation.walkthrough: Willingly means gladly in the surface, but the setter means added to a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A codicil is a supplement that amends or adds to a will after it has been made.

clue.text: Make garish design for each writer

indicators.note: to design is to lay out afresh, so the next word's letters are given a new layout

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
a pen is something you write with

explanation.surface: A brief to produce a gaudy design for every author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' looks like the noun after 'garish', but it is a verb working on 'each'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheapen something is to make it tawdry or vulgar in appearance, close to making it garish.

clue.text: Sleep! Son drops off? Rubbish!

indicators.note: a letter that drops off falls away from the word

blocks.note: slumber is sleep
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone nodding off is told to sleep, and dismisses the idea as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops off' suggests falling asleep; it is the instruction to take S off the start. Lumber is British for unwanted junk.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English lumber is disused furniture and junk stored away, i.e. rubbish.

clue.text: Still carrying the message that could widen up re-organisation

indicators.note: a reorganisation puts things into a fresh order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A memo that a broader restructuring might be on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition pictures a tape or disk that has not been erased, so the recording is still on it.
explanation.definitionFit: An unwiped tape or disk has not been erased, so the recorded message remains on it.

clue.text: Former member of the cast playing the heavy

blocks.note: ex means former
an actor is a member of a cast

explanation.surface: An ex-cast member is now cast as the villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The heavy' in theatre is the villain's role; here it means a demanding, oppressive person.
explanation.definitionFit: An exactor is someone who demands payment or obedience harshly, an oppressive enforcer like a heavy.

clue.text: Brown has turn to dance

blocks.note: tan is a brown colour
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Mr Brown gets his chance to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a Latin American ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: Bloomer to put trophy on goat

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting one thing on another places it after, so the trophy follows the goat

blocks.note: a goat butts, so it is a butter
a cup is a trophy

explanation.surface: Instructions for a blunder: plonking a trophy on a goat.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is both a blunder and, cryptically, a flower, something that blooms; and a goat is a 'butter' because it butts.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttercup is a yellow wild flower, and anything that blooms can be called a bloomer in crosswords.

clue.text: Leading evangelist ruined one nun out of boredom

indicators.note: the leading part of a word is its opening letter
something ruined is wrecked, its letters left in a new order

blocks.note: the first letter
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A star preacher has corrupted a nun out of sheer tedium.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a feeling of listlessness and weariness from lack of interest, a French loan for boredom.

clue.text: Unusual way to cook steak

blocks.note: first meaning: uncommon
second meaning: lightly cooked, red in the middle

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as if an odd cooking method is meant; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means scarce or uncommon, and also describes meat seared briefly so it stays red inside.

clue.text: Yearns for new style hero on the waterside

indicators.note: giving something a new style remodels it, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: to long for is to yearn
letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pines for a new kind of hero down by the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Longshore means found or employed along the shore, as in longshoreman, a docker working on the waterfront.
